stories.title: Selldorf Architects Renews 14K-SF 860 Broadway Lease for 10 Years
stories.excerpt: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects has renewed its 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease at Gordon Property Group’s 860 Broadway. Selldorf has called the Flatiron District’s 860 Broadway home for the last two decades, according to landlord brokerage Colliers. The asking rent was not disclosed. However, the average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $79.41 per square foot, with Class A office space asking an average of $97.22 per foot and Class B space asking $79.96 during the second quarter, according to Colliers data. Seth Hecht from Colliers represented Gordon Property in this deal, while the tenant was represented by Erik Schmall and Scott Weiss from Savills. “860 Broadway is one of Manhattan’s iconic office buildings, and its location continues to make it a highly desirable destination for creative and innovative companies,” Hecht said in a statement announcing the renewal. “When a firm as globally respected as Selldorf Architects commits to another decade in the building, it speaks to both the property’s enduring appeal and the long-term strength of this market.” Savills did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. “Our focus has always been on owning and operating buildings for the long term,” Tim Gordon, managing director of Gordon Property Group, said in the statement. “Creating an environment where great companies choose to stay and grow is the ultimate measure of our success, and we’re proud that 860 Broadway continues to earn that kind of commitment.” Selldorf Architects was founded by Annabelle Selldorf in New York City in 1988, according to the company website. The firm has worked on a number of prestigious projects, including the Frick Collection, the Chateau Haut-Brion — a 16th century estate near Bordeaux in France – and the Museum of Contemporary Art in San Diego. bullets: Selldorf Architects renews 14K-SF lease at 860 Broadway, Flatiron, Manhattan for 10 years.
Midtown South Class A office averaging $97.22/SF; Class B at $79.96/SF in Q2.
Architectural tenant commitment signals demand stability in Manhattan creative/office market.
stories.summary: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects renewed its 13,815-square-foot lease at 860 Broadway in Manhattan's Flatiron District for another decade, cementing a 20-year presence. Comparable Class A office space in Midtown South was trading at $97.22 per square foot and Class B at $79.96/SF in Q2. The renewal underscores sustained demand from creative/knowledge-work tenants for trophy Manhattan office addresses.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, the renewal signals stability in Manhattan's creative-sector employment hub; sustained office demand from high-wage, sticky tenants (architects, tech) supports underlying residential demand in proximate neighborhoods like Flatiron and NoMad. Office-to-residential conversion optionality remains if future office fundamentals weaken.

stories.title: Agora Delivers 90K-SF N. Las Vegas Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Agora Realty (Agora) has completed construction for Hylo Park South, its 90,750-square-foot grocery-anchored retail center located at the southeast corner of Lake Mead Blvd. and Rancho Drive in the city of North Las Vegas. This retail center will be a central gathering place for Agora’s 73-acre master-planned, mixed-use community Hylo Park that is now in its third phase of development with approximate construction costs of $375 million. The 11-acre retail center is already 95 percent leased to many nationally recognized tenants, led by anchor tenant Cardenas Markets along with Ross Dress for Less, Starbucks, Chipotle, In N Out, PDS Health, AT&T, UPS, Chase Bank, Allstate, Sourdough & Co., and Tesla. Hylo Park South tenants will be open and operating by early 2027. In addition, Agora sold a 1.2-acre pad within Hylo Park South at the southeast corner of Rancho Drive and Lake Mead Blvd. to In-N-Out Burger for development. The post Agora Delivers 90K-SF N. Las Vegas Retail Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Agora completed 90,750-SF retail center Hylo Park South in North Las Vegas; 95% leased.
73-acre mixed-use development at $375M total cost; phase 3 underway; 1.2 acres sold to In-N-Out.
Anchor tenants: Cardenas Markets, Ross, Chipotle, Tesla; opening early 2027.
stories.summary: Agora Realty completed Hylo Park South, a grocery-anchored 90,750-square-foot retail center at Lake Mead Boulevard and Rancho Drive in North Las Vegas, already 95% leased to national tenants including Cardenas Markets and Ross Dress for Less. The retail center is part of Agora's 73-acre mixed-use Hylo Park community, now in phase 3 with approximately $375 million in total construction costs. Tenants will open by early 2027.
stories.impact: Mixed-use master-planned communities anchored by grocery and retail density signal sustained residential demand in North Las Vegas submarket. Retail absorption and anchor leasing strength indicate consumer spending power and population density sufficient to support multifamily development; Agora's phased approach and institutional capital commitment de-risk residential delivery in the Vegas periphery. Monitor phase 2 residential absorption for confirmation of demand trajectory.

stories.title: BH Picks Up Nearly 300K-SF Plano Office Park
stories.excerpt: BH Properties, a value-add real estate investment firm with regional offices in Dallas, Austin, and Houston, completed the acquisition of Tollway North Office Park, a 297,591-square-foot, seven-building business park in Plano, Texas. The acquisition follows the firm’s February 2025 purchase of the adjacent R&D at Legacy campus, bringing BH’s ownership within the Legacy Business Park to more than 675,000 square feet across fourteen buildings. BH acquired the property from KBS. KBS was represented by Newmark’s Dallas team of Gary Carr, Chris Murphy, Robert Hill, and Austin Sheahan, while BH was represented by Scott Henry, its managing director of Texas acquisitions based in Dallas. The development was built between 1998 and 2000. BH Properties plans to capitalize on the property’s leasing upside while evaluating future repositioning opportunities that reflect changing occupier preferences. Stream Realty’s Chase Lopez, James Mantzuranis, and Sam Bass in Dallas will be representing BH on leasing. The post BH Picks Up Nearly 300K-SF Plano Office Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BH Properties acquired Tollway North Office Park, 297,591-SF, 7 buildings in Plano, Texas.
Purchase follows Feb 2025 R&D at Legacy acquisition; combined holdings now 675K+ SF across 14 buildings.
BH plans value-add repositioning to reflect changing occupier preferences; built 1998–2000.
stories.summary: BH Properties, a value-add specialist, completed acquisition of Tollway North Office Park, a 297,591-square-foot seven-building business park in Plano, Texas, from KBS. This follows BH's February 2025 purchase of the adjacent R&D at Legacy campus, bringing total Legacy Business Park holdings to over 675,000 square feet across 14 buildings. BH plans to pursue leasing upside and future repositioning aligned with evolving occupier preferences.
stories.impact: Consolidation of legacy business park assets in Plano signals optionality for future office-to-residential conversion or ground-up multifamily redevelopment as Plano's office-flex demand matures. BH's value-add platform and focus on repositioning suggest recognition that aging 1998–2000 vintage office space faces structural headwinds; proximity to Dallas-Fort Worth's core job centers makes land candidacy for high-density residential increasingly attractive. Watch for any future zoning or master-plan announcements.

stories.title: Cabot Offloads 2.4M-SF Texas Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Cabot Properties sold an eight-building modern industrial portfolio totaling approximately 2.4 million square feet across Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston, Texas. The portfolio was acquired by a private real estate investment firm. Five of the properties are in the Dallas-Fort Worth submarkets of South Dallas, Alliance, DFW Airport, and Great Southwest/Arlington with an average vintage of 2015, totaling approximately two million square feet. Sustained occupier demand, declining vacancy, and improving absorption across large-format industrial space have resulted in a recent period of accelerated leasing and transactional activity in the Dallas-Fort Worth market. The additional three buildings are in Houston’s Northwest and North Corridors. The Capital Markets Teams of CBRE, Cushman & Wakefield, and Eastdil Secured represented Cabot separately across the transaction. Last week, Cabot sold a collection of 11 industrial properties totaling approximately 2.5 million square feet across key industrial submarkets in Greater Chicago and Minneapolis, Minnesota. The post Cabot Offloads 2.4M-SF Texas Industrial Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Cabot Properties sold 2.4M-SF industrial portfolio (8 buildings) in DFW and Houston to private investor.
DFW: 2M SF across South Dallas, Alliance, DFW Airport, Great Southwest/Arlington; vintage ~2015.
Houston: 3 buildings in Northwest and North Corridors; sustained occupier demand, declining vacancy, strong absorption.
stories.summary: Cabot Properties sold an eight-building industrial portfolio totaling approximately 2.4 million square feet across Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston to a private real estate investment firm. Five properties (approximately 2 million square feet, average 2015 vintage) are in DFW submarkets including South Dallas, Alliance, DFW Airport, and Great Southwest/Arlington. Three additional buildings are in Houston's Northwest and North Corridors. The DFW market has experienced sustained occupier demand, declining vacancy, and accelerated leasing activity.
stories.impact: Cabot's divestiture of newer (2015-vintage) industrial in DFW likely signals capital redeployment or portfolio trimming at peak pricing and strong leasing momentum. DFW's sustained industrial demand and declining vacancy underscore robust logistics employment and inbound corporate activity, which supports concurrent residential demand in secondary/tertiary markets near industrial clusters (e.g., Alliance, DFW Airport corridors). Residential developers should monitor continued industrial absorption to validate job-growth assumptions for apartment demand modeling in outer DFW submarkets.

stories.title: Mortgage Bankers Association: CRE Lending Volume Up 16% Year-Over-Year
stories.excerpt: Commercial and multifamily mortgage loan originations were 16% higher in the second quarter of 2026 than in the year-ago period, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association’s (MBA) Quarterly Survey of Commercial/Multifamily Mortgage Bankers Originations. Dollar volume increased 12% from Q1 of 2026, MBA said. Increased originations for retail, office, hotel, industrial and multifamily properties led to an overall increase in commercial/multifamily lending volumes. Dollar volume of loans for retail properties rose 61%, while office loans rose 47%, lodging properties rose 19%, multifamily rose 8% and industrial increased 6%. Healthcare originations decreased 19% year-over-year. “Commercial and multifamily mortgage lending maintained its upward trajectory in the second quarter as improving capital markets and stronger transaction activity supported higher origination volumes,” said Reggie Booker, MBA’s associate VP of commercial research. “Office lending was strong, with increases in originations on an annual and quarterly basis, signaling renewed financing activity in a sector that has faced significant headwinds. Additionally, CMBS and bank lenders posted particularly strong gains in the second quarter. Although activity remains uneven across some capital sources and property sectors, the overall increase in lending points to continued improvement in commercial real estate finance markets.” The post Mortgage Bankers Association: CRE Lending Volume Up 16% Year-Over-Year appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MBA: Commercial/multifamily mortgage originations up 16% YoY in Q2 2026; up 12% QoQ.
Retail loans +61%, office +47%, lodging +19%, multifamily +8%, industrial +6% YoY.
Healthcare originations down 19% YoY; CMBS and bank lenders posted strong Q2 gains.
stories.summary: Commercial and multifamily mortgage loan originations rose 16% year-over-year in Q2 2026, with dollar volume up 12% sequentially, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association. Retail loans surged 61%, office 47%, lodging 19%, multifamily 8%, and industrial 6% on a year-over-year basis, while healthcare originations fell 19%. CMBS and bank lenders posted particularly strong gains, signaling renewed financing activity across property types.
stories.impact: Multifamily originations growing at only 8% YoY while retail, office, and lodging surge 47–61% suggests capital is flowing disproportionately to repositioning/recovery plays in distressed sectors, not new multifamily supply. Modest 8% growth implies tightening construction financing availability relative to demand, favoring well-capitalized developers and sponsors with existing relationships and strong leverage metrics. Cap rate compression risk if rates stabilize; developers must lock construction debt before further rate normalization.

stories.title: Valley National Bank Provides $30M Value-Add Refi for Park Towers in Miami
stories.excerpt: Moshe Popack’s YMP Real Estate Management has secured $30 million to refinance Park Towers, a 210-unit multifamily complex in Miami, Commercial Observer can first report. Valley National Bank provided the loan, structured at a fixed-rate of 6.09 percent, while Meridian Capital Group’s David Hayum and Michael Farkovits arranged the transaction. Meridian’s Hyum noted in a statement that Popack, a third-generation real estate investor, and the YMP management team have owned and operated Park Towers for more than a decade and have engaged in a concentrated value-add strategy, investing capital improvements into the property for several years. “Valley National Bank recognized that track record, stayed engaged throughout the process, and delivered a financing solution that met the borrower’s objectives,” added Hyum. Park Towers is located at 777 North West 155th Lane in the Biscayne Gardens section of Miami, near both University of Miami and Florida International University. The 224,519-square-foot apartment building opened in 1973. The 10-story building is a mix of studios, one-bedrooms and two-bedrooms and has undergone capital improvements since YMP purchased the asset in 2012. YMP Management has emerged as a player in the Sun Belt in recent years and now owns more than 4,000 multifamily units across Florida, Georgia and North Carolina. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Valley National Bank provided $30M refi for Park Towers, 210-unit multifamily in Miami at 6.09% fixed.
YMP Real Estate Management (owner, 10+ years) pursued concentrated value-add strategy with capital improvements.
Property located near University of Miami and Florida International University in Biscayne Gardens.
stories.summary: YMP Real Estate Management secured $30 million in refinance financing from Valley National Bank for Park Towers, a 210-unit multifamily complex in Miami's Biscayne Gardens section, at a fixed rate of 6.09 percent. The borrower, a third-generation real estate investor, has owned and operated the property for over a decade while executing a value-add capital improvement strategy. The property is proximate to both University of Miami and Florida International University.
stories.impact: Value-add refi at 6.09% fixed signals lender conviction in Miami multifamily fundamentals and sustained income growth trajectory post-improvement. Proximity to FIU and UM validates strong institutional tenant demand (student/faculty housing) and demographic stability. However, 6.09% refi rate underscores that new construction financing will remain elevated; developers targeting Miami should focus on ground-lease or partnership structures to improve levered returns and absorb higher cost of capital.

stories.title: RXR-Led Team Lands Construction Financing for 301-Unit Denver Rental Community
stories.excerpt: RXR, together with Halpern Real Estate Investments, Korman Communities and Invent Development Partners, secured $125 million in construction financing for AVE Station House, a 301-unit luxury multifamily development in Denver, Colorado. The property was financed with a $100 million senior loan from Madison Realty Capital and a $25 million mezzanine loan from an insurance company. The development comprises 271 market-rate apartments and 30 affordable units, along with more than 6,200 square feet of ground-floor retail space and approximately 290 secured parking spaces. Upon completion, AVE Station House will offer a mix of studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and three-bedroom residences. Each apartment will feature work-from-home spaces. Residents will have access to an extensive amenity package including a rooftop pool and lounge, fitness center, spa with sauna and steam. JLL Capital Markets’ Debt Advisory team, led by Leon McBroom, Michael Gigliotti, Will Haass and Ellie Savage, represented the borrower, as well as Paul Patafio of Hudson Realty Capital, who represented the borrower in arranging financing for the project The post RXR-Led Team Lands Construction Financing for 301-Unit Denver Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RXR/Halpern/Korman/Invent secured $125M construction financing for AVE Station House, Denver, 301 units.
$100M senior from Madison Realty Capital; $25M mezz from insurance company; 271 market-rate + 30 affordable.
6,200 SF retail, 290 parking spaces; mix of studios to 3-bedrooms with work-from-home spaces.
stories.summary: A development team including RXR, Halpern Real Estate Investments, Korman Communities, and Invent Development Partners secured $125 million in construction financing for AVE Station House, a 301-unit luxury multifamily development in Denver. The financing comprises a $100 million senior loan from Madison Realty Capital and a $25 million mezzanine loan from an insurance company. The project includes 271 market-rate units, 30 affordable units, 6,200 square feet of ground-floor retail, and approximately 290 parking spaces.
stories.impact: Successful securitization of multifamily construction in Denver by top-tier sponsors signals sustained investor appetite for luxury rental in West Coast markets, despite broader economic uncertainty. $125M raise for 301 units (~$415K per unit) implies strong cost basis and sponsor equity; insurance company mezz participation (vs. mezzanine specialists) shows institutional capital re-entering development stack. Denver's strong job growth and in-migration continue to support premium rental fundamentals; expect competing starts in QOZ/transit-adjacent submarkets where land remains available.

stories.title: Document Processing Platform Extend AI Signs 9K-SF Lease at 119 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: An artificial intelligence-driven document processing firm is relocating within the Flatiron District, Commercial Observer has learned Extend AI signed an 8,750-square-foot lease across the entire sixth floor of 119 Fifth Avenue in a relocation from its current offices at 135 West 29th Street, according to the brokers at Nomad Group. Nomad did not disclose the length of the lease, but said asking rent for the building, which property records indicate is owned by the Haddad family, was $105 per square foot. “The companies actually building the future of AI are not abandoning the office — they are raising the bar for it,” Nomad’s Nick Hein, who represented the tenant in the transaction, said in a statement. “119 Fifth Avenue offered Extend the character, status and proximity to an established tech ecosystem that includes Microsoft, Adyen, Legora, Clay and many others, along with a HQ equal to the scale of what they’re building.” Bill Janetschek and Matthew DeRose, also from Nomad Group, negotiated on behalf of the landlord. The building from 1906 is at the corner of Fifth Avenue and East 19th Street, within the Ladies’ Mile Historic District and several blocks south of Extend AI’s current headquarters north of Madison Square Park, an area that has been a major destination for AI firms. As recently as late July, AI data platform Chalk signed a lease for 26,607 square feet at Castro Properties’ 43 West 23rd Street, while on Thursday CO reported that AI-driven employee management platform Warp expanded to 24,500 square feet at HRC’s 156 Fifth Avenue. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Extend AI (AI document processing) leased 8,750-SF sixth floor at 119 Fifth Avenue, Flatiron, Manhattan.
Relocation from 135 West 29th Street; asking rent $105/SF; building built 1906, owned by Haddad family.
Tenant cites proximity to tech ecosystem: Microsoft, Adyen, Legora, Clay in Flatiron.
stories.summary: Extend AI, an artificial intelligence-driven document processing firm, leased 8,750 square feet on the entire sixth floor of 119 Fifth Avenue in Flatiron, Manhattan, at $105 per square foot, relocating from 135 West 29th Street. The 1906-built building, owned by the Haddad family, offered the tenant proximity to an established tech ecosystem including Microsoft, Adyen, Legora, and Clay, plus office space befitting the firm's growth scale.
stories.impact: AI and tech-services tenants remain anchored to Flatiron/NoMad, validating cluster economics and justifying premium $105/SF rents for office space. Tenant's stated rationale ('HQ equal to the scale of what they're building') signals class-A office scarcity and premium pricing power in trophy submarkets. For multifamily developers: sustained high-wage tech employment in Flatiron supports elevated rents in adjacent residential; conversion plays on aging office stock remain viable if vacancy tightens further.

stories.title: Tishman Speyer’s 6 Grand Central Hits the Market for Roughly $450M
stories.excerpt: Fancy adding a 770,386-square-foot trophy office property to your portfolio? You’re in luck. Tishman Speyer is marketing 6 Grand Central for sale, sources told Commercial Observer, with an asking price somewhere around $450 million. The fee simple interest in the property is being marketed by Eastdil Secured’s Gary Phillips and Will Silverman, sources said. The Class A office tower is at the corner of Third Avenue and East 42nd Street in the Grand Central submarket with a direct connection to Grand Central Terminal via the Chrysler Building. The building is one of only four postwar buildings with such access. Formerly known as 666 Third Avenue, the property was bought by Tishman in 1998. It was last renovated in 2022, and rebranded as 6 Grand Central in 2024 “to reflect our dedication to grandeur and excellence, and the building’s direct connection to Grand Central Terminal,” according to a LinkedIn post from the firm. That same year, investment manager VanEck signed a 10-year renewal for its 53,333 square feet on the entire ninth and part of the eighth floor of the building. Other tenants include the Consulate General of the Netherlands, law firm Mintz Levin and health care logistics firm Strata Critical. Studio Grand Central occupies the sixth floor, offering coworking spaces, private offices and meeting rooms. Earlier this year, Tishman also parted ways with CitySpire, a 70-story office and condo tower on West 56th Street, selling the property to DelShah Capital for $135.7 million. Tishman Speyer declined to comment. Cathy Cunningham can be reached at ccunningham@commercialobserver.com,
bullets: Tishman Speyer marketing 6 Grand Central (770,386 SF) for ~$450M; fee simple interest via Eastdil.
Class A office at Third Ave & East 42nd St, Grand Central submarket; direct Terminal access (one of 4).
Property renovated 2022, rebranded 2024; VanEck renewed 53,333 SF (9th & part 8th floor) for 10 years.
stories.summary: Tishman Speyer is marketing 6 Grand Central, a 770,386-square-foot Class A office tower at Third Avenue and East 42nd Street in Manhattan's Grand Central submarket, for approximately $450 million. The property, formerly known as 666 Third Avenue and acquired by Tishman in 1998, was last renovated in 2022 and rebranded in 2024 to emphasize its direct connection to Grand Central Terminal (one of only four postwar buildings with such access). Tenant VanEck recently renewed its 53,333-square-foot footprint for 10 years.
stories.impact: Tishman's $450M ask for trophy Grand Central office reflects capital recycling in an uncertain office market despite recent CMBS strength (per Article 5). Institutional tenant renewal (VanEck, 10-year) masks structural challenges in the broader Manhattan office stock. For multifamily: if 6 Grand Central or similar trophy assets trade below replacement cost or are repurposed, conversion risk could accelerate in Midtown submarkets with high-density zoning, adding supply pressure to adjacent residential markets.

stories.title: Bridge Investment Group Provides $67M Refi for Value-Add Multifamily Outside Boston
stories.excerpt: Invictus Real Estate Partners has secured $67.2 million to refinance Eliot on Ocean, a 194-unit multifamily property in Revere Beach, Mass., a coastal submarket five miles outside of Boston. Bridge Investment Group Holdings provided the debt, structured as a three-year, floating-rate loan, while a JLL Capital Markets team of Scott Aiese, Tom Sullivan and Alex Staikos arranged the transaction. In a statement, Aiese spoke to the asset’s “irreplaceable location,” particularly because of the property’s transit connectivity, and noted that the deal is a value-add play for the sponsor who aims to capture higher market rents through capital improvements. “Revere Beach represents one of the few remaining value-add opportunities in Boston’s constrained waterfront multifamily market,” said Aiese, who noted that the Revere Beach market has received more than $1 billion in institutional investment since 2015. Located at 660 Ocean Avenue in Revere Beach — a three-mile waterfront corridor that is home to the first public beach in the United States — the seven-story Eliot on Ocean spans 143,252 square feet and opened in 2016. Aside from offering residents direct access to the beach, the apartment complex sits directly on the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority’s Wonderland Blue Line station, offering a trip into Downtown Boston in less than 35 minutes. Invictus Real Estate Partners plans to improve the lobby and shared amenity spaces and improve appliances and finishes throughout the complex, according to JLL. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bridge Investment Group provided $67.2M refi for Eliot on Ocean, 194-unit multifamily in Revere Beach, Mass.
Three-year floating-rate loan; property 5 miles outside Boston, waterfront location with transit connectivity.
Value-add sponsor targeting higher market rents via capital improvements; Revere Beach received $1B+ institutional investment since 2015.
stories.summary: Invictus Real Estate Partners secured $67.2 million in refinance financing from Bridge Investment Group Holdings for Eliot on Ocean, a 194-unit multifamily property in Revere Beach, Massachusetts, a coastal submarket five miles outside Boston. The loan is structured as a three-year floating-rate facility. The sponsor is pursuing a value-add strategy to capture higher market rents through capital improvements, leveraging the property's irreplaceable waterfront location and transit connectivity. Revere Beach has attracted over $1 billion in institutional investment since 2015.
stories.impact: Revere Beach's $1B+ institutional investment and value-add financing success signal strong Boston-area residential demand extending beyond core urban markets into secondary coastal corridors with transit access. Three-year floating-rate structure reflects Bridge's confidence in rate stability and rent-growth trajectory. For developers: Boston's constrained multifamily supply and limited waterfront inventory create scarcity value; coastal submarkets within 5–7 miles of downtown (Cambridge, Somerville, Revere) remain target for mid-rise development. Monitor transit improvements and income growth in nearby Route 128 tech corridor to validate demand elasticity.
